text:
elaine: hitting a confusing failure in py-sdk 0.7.3 (async via httpx). upstream returns 422 text/plain 'email required' but SDK tries to json.loads and raises JSONDecodeError -> we catch and re-raise RedwoodAPIError with zero context: no .http_status, no raw body, nothing useful. this breaks our onboarding sample app which surfaces a generic 'API error' to users. any fix suggestions?

zhou: is this specific to httpx async client? can you paste the small repro + exception attributes you see?

elaine: yes httpx async. repro:```py
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=...) as c:
    await c.accounts.create({"name": "Acme"})  # staging returns 422 text/plain
```
exception in logs: `RedwoodAPIError: failed to parse error payload` and `hasattr(e, 'http_status')` is False. headers show `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body `email required`.

pete: we added richer error metadata for sync/requests paths earlier, but the httpx async wrapper never copied the metadata onto the raised exception. simple fix: always read the raw response bytes first, attach metadata to the error object, then attempt JSON parse. preserve the original parse error as __cause__ so traces remain helpful.

maya: +1. proposal details: on non-success responses do: read raw = await resp.aread() (httpx) or resp.read() (aiohttp), set err.http_status = resp.status_code, err.raw_bytes = raw, try decode to err.raw_body using resp.encoding or 'utf-8' errors='replace', only attempt json.loads when content-type contains 'json' or raw_body.lstrip().startswith(('{','[')). If parse fails set err.parsed_json = None and chain cause. Then raise err with metadata attached.

elaine: that would let our sample app inspect e.http_status and e.raw_body and show a friendly validation message instead of the generic one. exactly what we need.

zhou: typing: update the stub so RedwoodAPIError has Optional[int] http_status, Optional[str] raw_body, Optional[bytes] raw_bytes, Optional[dict] parsed_json. Also add a method `get_json()` that returns parsed_json or raises a clear MessageParseError. This will make DX better for teams using mypy in onboarding samples.

pete: for backwards compat, keep `.body` as an alias property for now but emit DeprecationWarning in docs. also adjust __str__ to avoid emitting huge bodies (truncate to 1500 chars). add unit to assert truncation.

maya: tests to add: 1) httpx unit that fakes a 422 text/plain response and asserts e.http_status == 422 and e.raw_body == 'email required'; 2) binary/gzip body preserved in raw_bytes and raw_body==None if decoding fails; 3) mypy stub test to ensure attributes exist; 4) small integration test against staging that reproduces the onboarding sample flow.

ci-bot: CI: branch httpx-async-error-meta (tests + mypy + lint)  failing mypy on stubs <https://ci.internal/py-sdk/9999|details>

pete: i'll open the patch PR and target 0.7.4. small nit: some proxies return HTML pages that include JSON snippets; prefer content-type sniffing + a quick startswith check rather than blind json attempt to avoid false positives.

elaine: noted, also update SDK docs in errors.rst with a short example showing robust handling in onboarding sample app:```py
try:
    await client.accounts.create(data)
except RedwoodAPIError as e:
    if e.http_status == 422:
        # prefer parsed_json when present
        details = e.parsed_json or e.raw_body
        show_user_friendly_error(details)
    else:
        raise
```

zhou: all good. @pete please include changelog entry and mention the new attributes in the migration guide.

pete: will do. pinging @maya for review when PR ready.

elaine: thanks folks, this should fix the onboarding UX regression that blocked a demo yesterday. curl to reproduce locally: `curl -i -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/accounts -d '{"name":"x"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"` (on our staging proxy returns 422 text/plain).

maya: :thumbsup:
